newsitem.title: UK: Most Eurobourses track Dow up, dlr nervous.
newsitem.headline: Most Eurobourses track Dow up, dlr nervous.

text.p: Most European bourses were higher following back-to-back days of record closes on Wall Street and a near steady U.S. blue chip opening on Friday.

U.S. stocks mostly led a worldwide rally in stocks this week, racking up hefty gains from post-U.S. election euphoria, a positive earnings outlook from heavy-weight Intel Corp and lower long-term rates in the U.S. bond market.

But "Wall Street has gained around 130 points in two days and it may take a bit of a breather...if it corrects heavily, we may come off a little," said a senior equities trader in London about the blue-chip FTSE-100 index.

Further pressure on U.S. stocks could also emerge as the dollar continued to look shaky. Though the dollar rose from Thursday's low with help from rising stock and government bond prices and remarks from Japanese officials, dealers expected "I think the dollar is likely to fall as far as 110.00 yen next week as a downward correction of the recent rally close to 115 yen," said a currency manager at a Japanese bank in Tokyo.
Dealers remained wary of a policy shift despite remarks from a Japanese economy minister that Japanese rates must be kept low for now.

A Japanese finance minister's comments that he was not worried about the current foreign exchange market and the Japanese government should not intervene also did little to soothe nerves after Thursday's dollar drop of some two-yen.
Germany's DAX index of 30 leading shares closed bourse trade at a record high 2,739.83.

Dresdner Bank, Germany's third largest commercial bank, stood among the biggest gainers in the DAX. Dresdner shares soared more than three percent to a year high on news it plans to merge its global funds business. U.S. investment bank Salomon Bros also reiterated its buy recommendation on Dresdner.

In Paris, the blue-chip CAC-40 slipped into negative territory after a positive start as investors sold some shares to lock in some profits made during the index's near eight-percent run to about two-year highs this week. Investors were also squaring books before a three-day holiday weekend.
On Monday, France and Belgium celebrate Armistice Day and the U.S. celebrates Veteran's Day.

Dutch shares were boosted by strong third-quarter earnings from Unilever and accelerated by some money mangers who, surprised by the market's strength, were forced to quickly buy shares so as not to miss the entire move up.
"Some people are having to pay up for stock they could have got a guilder cheaper yesterday," a Dutch dealer said.
British stocks rose, but the outlook was clouded by inflation and interest rate fears.

The Confederation of British Industry said in a report that British retail sales for October rose at the fastest rate since 1988, which highlighted again the Bank of England's forecast on Wednesday that inflation and interest rates were set to rise.
"With inflation fears around, people are still scared this market will crack," said a senior equities dealer.
London traders were also expected to stay sidelined before the policy-setting meeting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee on November 13, followed by the UK budget on November 26.

"Consensus is still for no change (in U.S. rates), but the worry is that we are at the bottom of the rate cycle in the U.S. It's just a question of when a rate rise comes through," said SG Strauss Turnbull strategist Andy Hartwill.
Further worries that could cap gains on London's blue-chips came from sterling's recent surge, prompting fears the strong currency will start to carve into corporate earnings.
By 1510 GMT, sterling was at $1.6460, just softer than $1.6481 in late European trading on Thursday.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5057 marks and 111.55 yen, compared with 1.5073 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1600 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 8.1 points higher at 3,908.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 7.17 at 2,206.64
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index rose 26.61 to 2,739.83.
PRECIOUS METALS At 1515 GMT
Afternoon gold was fixed just easier at $378.15 from $378.35 earlier. Silver shed a cent to $4.79.
